name: the Garden
title: 🌿 The Garden
blurb: The Garden is alive, and it remembers. Flowers move when no wind blows, paths lead where they shouldn't, and the Reflection Pool whispers things nobody told it.

atmospheres.text: The air smells of rain that hasn't fallen yet.
Everything is very still, as if the Garden is holding its breath.
Bees drone lazily from bloom to bloom.
Sunlight falls in long gold stripes through the leaves.
A warm breeze carries the smell of crushed mint.
Somewhere nearby, water is laughing over stones.
The moon hangs low enough to touch.
Fireflies drift up out of the grass like sparks that forgot to go out.
Your footsteps make no sound at all.
The shadows here are a little longer than the light should allow.
A cold wind moves through the leaves, but nothing else stirs.
For a moment, every leaf turns to face you.
Mist curls low over the ground, knee-deep and slow.
The stars are unusually bright tonight, and there seem to be more of them.
Dew beads on every petal, catching the light.
An owl calls once, then thinks better of it.
The glass panes hum faintly, like a finger around a wine glass.
It smells of old paper and wet stone.
The Garden feels busy today, full of small invisible errands.
Something rustles just beyond the edge of the path.
The roses are unusually fragrant, almost dizzying.
A single leaf falls, very slowly, and never quite lands.
The ground is warm underfoot, like something beneath it is sleeping.
Distant bells ring out, though Velmora has no bells that sound like that.
The water is perfectly still, and the reflection in it is not quite yours.
A thin, silver light clings to the edges of everything.
The wind carries voices, too faint to make out.
Butterflies settle on the path ahead, as if waiting for you.
The temperature drops sharply, just for a breath.
The whole Garden smells, impossibly, of fresh bread.
The lanterns flicker in a pattern that's almost a word.
Petals drift down from a tree that isn't blooming.
Clouds gather overhead, but only overhead of you.
The ivy on the walls has grown since this morning. You can tell.
It's warm and green and perfectly peaceful.
Crickets sing in perfect time with each other.
Every flower in sight has turned black.
The petals are black as ink, and the air tastes of ash.
The Ancient Tree's glow reaches even here, gold and green.
The air is thick with moon moths, silver wings everywhere you look.

outcomes.text: The vines draw quietly aside to let you pass.
A flower opens beneath your hand as you reach out.
The Garden hums, very softly, as though it's pleased you came.
Petals settle on your shoulders like a welcome.
The path ahead seems to lean toward you.
You get the distinct feeling you are being looked after.
Something beneath the soil remembers you. Fondly.
The roses bow, just slightly, as you go by.
A warm breeze follows you for a while.
The grass springs back behind you faster than it should.
A bird lands on a branch beside you and stays.
The light shifts to show you something you'd have missed.
A thorn that was about to catch your sleeve pulls itself back.
The Garden seems to be in a generous mood.
As you approach, the flowers close around you.
The Garden carries on with its business, as if you're not quite there.
A leaf lands on your head. It might have been an accident.
Nothing else happens, which somehow feels deliberate.
You have the feeling you've been noticed.
A sprinkler of dew goes off, perfectly aimed at your shoes.
The moment passes. The Garden moves on. So do you.
Somewhere, something makes a note of your visit.
The roses turn their faces away as you pass.
A bramble snags your robe and doesn't let go straight away.
The path is a little longer on the way back than it was on the way in.
Every bloom within reach snaps shut.
The Garden goes very quiet while you're here.
The birds stop singing until you leave.
Something beneath the soil remembers you.
The vines tighten across the path. You find another way.
A cold wind pushes you, gently but firmly, toward the gate.
Every rose snaps shut at once. The sound is like a door slamming.
The ground is hard and unfriendly, and your footprints fill with water.
You hear, very clearly, the Garden sigh.
The black petals rustle as you pass, like whispering.
A moth lands on your hand and stays there, glowing.
The Tree's light brushes your face, warm as summer.

strange_house: The Garden rearranges the path behind you, just to see what you'll do.
Every flower you pass turns to follow you. All of them. Slowly.
The hedges hum your House's name.
You're sure the statues were facing the other way a moment ago.
Something plucks a single thread from your sleeve and keeps it.
The Garden seems very interested in you today. Unsettlingly so.

feed_good: {The} accepts your offering and nuzzles your hand before vanishing.
{The} eats from your palm, then leaves something behind in thanks.
feed_meh: {The} sniffs your offering, considers it, and walks off with it without a word.
follow_good: You follow {the} deeper in than you've ever been, until it stops and shows you something.
{The} leads you to a place you've never seen - and then it's gone.
follow_lost: You follow {the} for what feels like an hour. When you look up, you're back at the gate.
steal_good: You snatch it and run. {The} doesn't chase you. That's somehow worse.
steal_caught: {The} is quicker than you. Much quicker. You leave with nothing but a scratch - and the Garden saw.
leave: You let {the} be. As you go, you feel the Garden watching - approvingly, you think.
You step softly around {the} and carry on. Nothing is taken. Nothing is owed.
tend: You clear the weeds, loosen the soil, and give it a little water. The Garden notices.
You kneel and tend it carefully. Somewhere behind you, a flower that was closed opens.
You straighten a bent stem and pat the earth down. It seems to stand a little taller.
uproot: You tear it up by the roots. The Garden goes silent around you. It will remember this.
It comes up easily - too easily. The soil where it grew turns grey.
You rip it out and pocket what's useful. Every leaf nearby turns away from you.

offer_lines.full: The Garden accepts your offering without comment. It has had enough gifts from you for one day.
warm: The soil takes your offering gently. A flower you haven't seen before opens nearby.
The Garden accepts. Somewhere, a bird starts singing.
Your offering sinks into the earth, and the ground feels warmer where it went.
cold: The earth swallows your offering. The Garden says nothing. It noticed, though.
The roots draw your offering down into the dark. A little of the chill goes out of the air.
Your offering is gone the moment you look away. That's a start.

uses.response: 🗺️ You unfold the scrap and follow it - left at the statue, through the ferns, three steps past the dry well - to a patch of soil nobody has touched in a century. Something is waiting in it.
🗝️ You try the key in the old gate, the glasshouse door, the gardener's shed. It fits none of them. Whatever it opens, it isn't here.
💧 You pour the pool water back where it came from. For a moment the surface shows words - and then a leaf drifts up, with those same words in its veins.
🌟 You plant the starseed. Nothing happens. Then, very slowly, a single silver shoot turns - not toward the sun, but toward where the stars will be tonight.
🌰 You tuck the snoring acorn among the Ancient Tree's roots. The snoring stops. The Tree creaks, once, like a sigh of relief, and drops something at your feet.

reveals.beloved: 🌿 *The vines draw back from the path as you approach. A flower opens where your hand rests. The Garden has decided you should know: **it likes you.***
reveals.friendly: 🌸 *For the first time, a bloom turns toward you when you pass. The Garden has started to notice you - kindly.*
reveals.wary: 🥀 *The roses close as you pass. It's the first time you've noticed. It won't be the last.*
reveals.hostile: 🌑 *Something beneath the soil remembers you. The Garden has decided you should know that, too.*

events.title: A Door Behind the Roses
events.start: A door has appeared behind the roses. Old wood, iron hinges, no handle. Nobody remembers it being there.
events.end: The door behind the roses is gone. Just roses now. As if it never was.

events.title: The Flowers Turn Black
events.start: Every flower in the Garden has turned black. Nobody knows why. The Garden isn't saying.
events.end: Colour creeps back into the petals, one flower at a time. Whatever it was has passed.

events.title: The Golden Frog
events.start: A golden frog has set up shop by the water, and it's offering trades. Bring it something. It might give you something back.
events.end: The golden frog packs up its tiny stall and hops away. Business, apparently, is concluded.

events.title: A Name From the Pool
events.start: The Reflection Pool is whispering a name. **{name}**. Over and over, very softly.
events.end: The Pool goes quiet. Whatever it wanted to say, it has stopped saying it.

events.title: The Ancient Tree Glows
events.start: The Ancient Tree has begun to glow, gold and green, from the roots up. The whole Garden feels warmer.
events.end: The Tree's glow fades back into ordinary bark. It hums, once, and falls silent.

events.title: The Moon Moths
events.start: Hundreds of moon moths have poured out of nowhere. The Garden is silver with them.
events.end: The moon moths lift all at once and are gone, leaving silver dust on everything.

events.title: A Key Beneath the Bench
events.start: Someone has spotted a strange key beneath a bench in the Garden. It's still there. For now.
events.end: The key beneath the bench is gone. Somebody took it - or something did.

events.title: An Unexplored Path
events.start: A new path has opened in the Garden, winding somewhere nobody has been. The hedges on either side are very, very quiet.
events.end: The unexplored path has closed over. Ivy where the gap was. Did anyone see where it went?

events.title: The Garden Takes an Interest
events.start: The Garden is behaving very strangely toward **House {house}**. Flowers follow them. Paths shift. Nobody can say why.
events.end: The Garden seems to have lost interest in House {house}. For now.

secrets.response: 🐺 You howl. For a long moment, nothing. Then, from deep in the brambles, something howls back - and a crown of thorns rolls out onto the path.
🦌 You bow. When you look up, a stag is standing at the edge of the meadow. It bows back - and is gone.
🐘 You cup the broken stem in your hands. It straightens. It blooms. Every flower nearby turns to look at you.

phrases: i read the stars in the pool
chart the stars in the reflection pool
secrets.response: 🔭 You trace the reflected stars with a fingertip. They're not tonight's stars - they're a sky from centuries ago, and one of them is labelled in handwriting.

phrases: i test a hypothesis on the moonblooms
i run an experiment in the garden
secrets.response: 🌕 You change one variable - just one - and every moonbloom in the meadow changes colour to match. The Garden, it seems, likes a good experiment.

phrases: i ask the garden for a gift
secrets.response: 🌿 The Garden has been waiting for you to ask. A single white orchid grows up out of the path, opens, and lets itself be picked.
🥀 You say it out loud. The roses don't open. But the thorns across the path pull back, just a little.

phrases: i ask the pool a question
secrets.response: 💧 The Pool knows your name now, so it answers. It shows you a corridor in the Library you've never walked down, and a cabinet with a very small keyhole.

phrases: i press my ear to the ancient tree
secrets.response: 🌳 You press your ear to the bark. Deep inside, slow as centuries, something is **counting**. It gets to a number, stops, and starts again. You think it's counting students.

phrases: i say my name to the pool
whisper my name into the pool
secrets.response: 💧 You whisper your name into the Reflection Pool. It whispers back a different one. You don't know it. Yet.
🌹 The roses, one by one, turn to face you. It's a little unnerving. It's also, you think, polite.

phrases: i step into the mushroom ring
secrets.response: 🍄 You step inside the ring. The world goes quiet and very green. When you step out, your pockets are heavier and your shoes are on the wrong feet.
🌸 You sing, softly. Every moonbloom in the meadow opens at once, and one of them lets go a petal straight into your hand.
☀️ The sundial resists, then gives. For one second, every shadow in the Garden jumps an hour. Somewhere, a bell rings that shouldn't.

phrases: i knock on the gardener's shed
knock three times on the shed
secrets.response: 🏚️ You knock. From inside, someone knocks back - three times. The door stays shut. Under it, someone slides out a folded scrap of map.

phrases: i place a crystal in the stone hand
put a crystal in the stone hand
secrets.response: 🗿 You place it in the statue's palm. The fingers close, very slowly, and when they open again there's something else in them.
🦉 The owl looks at you for a long time. Then it says - clearly, in words - *"You're the first to ask."* It will not say anything else. Ever.

phrases: i walk through the willow door
secrets.response: 🌿 You step through the woven willow doorway and out the other side - into the same Garden, but quieter, and a little bit older. When you look back, you're somehow in front of the doorway again.

phrases: i knock on the door behind the roses
open the door behind the roses
secrets.response: 🚪 You knock. The door doesn't open - but beneath it, something slides out toward your feet.

phrases: i trade with the golden frog
secrets.response: FROG_TRADE
🗝️ You kneel and take the key from beneath the bench. It's heavier than it looks - and very, very cold.
🌿 You follow the new path through the hedge. It winds and winds, and at its end there's something waiting, as if left for you.
POOL_ANSWER

phrases: put my hand on the tree
secrets.response: 🌳 The glow runs up your arm like warm water. For a heartbeat, you can hear every root in the Garden.
